title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with new partnerships and budget allocations, while some projects are still struggling to meet deadlines. As the landscape evolves, both commercial and defense sectors are adjusting to emerging technologies and geopolitical pressures.

themes.title: European Firms Join NASA Program
themes.body: NASA's inclusion of three European companies in its commercial data program signals a growing trend of transatlantic collaboration in space. This move could enhance data-sharing capabilities and stimulate innovation across the Atlantic.

themes.title: Defense Budget Boosts Space Resilience
themes.body: The proposed $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for space resilience reflects a heightened focus on safeguarding U.S. interests in orbit. As threats evolve, this funding could bolster capabilities against emerging challenges.

themes.title: Hypersonic Tests Continue to Lag
themes.body: The repeated delays of hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this critical area. With three consecutive slips, stakeholders may need to reassess timelines and expectations.

themes.title: New Collaborations in Space Tech
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris's joint bid for a tactical SDA constellation highlights the increasing importance of collaboration in defense tech. Meanwhile, the agreement between Novaspace and others to create a global space capability dashboard suggests a push for comprehensive situational awareness.
